name: WSW Championship
notes: Reigns 1-5 are narrated, undated, on the promotion's own August 8, 2002 broadcast; no exact date for any of them survives.
epitaph: Wrestling's own top prize named on Western States Wrestling's broadcasts, its early lineage narrated on the promotion's own August 2002 video package: Thug Life won it first in a six-man elimination match, and it passed through The Mutt, Donovan Astros, Alternativ and “Electric” Evan Sky before “Superstar” Sean Southward's own long reign, defended without loss through every show of its 2002 run.

name: WSW Interstate Championship
epitaph: Founded at Retribution when Mr. Ed beat “Stunning” Steve Southward to become the last WSW Intercontinental Champion and the first Interstate Champion, the title changed hands twice more that summer before the promotion's own broadcasts left its final holder in dispute.

name: WSW Pacific Northwest Championship
epitaph: Founded at Retribution when Dean King beat Diablo in the WSW European Championship's own final match, the title passed to Jason Reynolds that July and stayed with him, unbeaten, for the rest of the promotion's 2002 run.

name: WSW Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Already held by Rukus The Luv Train when Western States Wrestling's 2002 run opens, the title changed hands once, to Knuckles at Retribution, and survived a Summer Showdown draw with Kendo Nakamura undecided.

name: WSW Television Championship
epitaph: Already held by Nemesis, its second-most-prestigious title in the promotion's own words, when Western States Wrestling's 2002 run opens, it changed hands twice: to “Kid Dynamic” that June and to Kano that July, who defended it for the rest of that run.

name: WSW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Vacated when its holders, Ionik, announced their in-storyline departure at Retribution, the New Midnight Express won and held it for the rest of the promotion's 2002 run.

name: WSW North American Championship
epitaph: Retired as a defended championship at Retribution, when Krim'nal became its last champion; the promotion's own 2004 return still called him “the last North American Champion before the shutdown,” unbeaten for it across its whole 2002 run.

name: WSW Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Two rival Hardcore titles were unified and retired in one cage battle royal at Retribution, its last champion, Nova Johnson, handing the belt itself to Kano backstage that June as a gesture, never revived as a defended championship in the promotion's 2002 run.
